entries.title: Internal Architecture: Tokenization, Normalization & Validation | Bank Statement Parser
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Architecture & Pipeline Specifications

Bank Statement Parser implements a deterministic, four-stage extraction and validation pipeline.

+------------------+ +-------------------+ +---------------------+ +--------------------+ | 1. Stream Ingest | --> | 2. Layout Tokenizer| --> | 3. Field Normalizer | --> | 4. Schema Validator| | (PDF/CSV/OFX) | | (Spatial Extraction)| | (Date/Amount/IBAN) | | (JSON / ISO 20022) | +------------------+ +-------------------+ +---------------------+ +--------------------+
  1. Stream Ingestion: Zero-copy memory mapping of input statement bytes.
  2. Layout Tokenization: Spatial bounding-box and tabular coordinate mapping.
  3. Field Normalization: Canonical standardization of transaction codes, currencies, and dates.
  4. Schema Validation: Mathematical checksum balance verification.

Contributing to Bank Statement Parser

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Bank Statement Parser. We welcome pull requests for new bank dialect parsers, performance optimizations, and documentation improvements.

Development Workflow

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ): Bank Statement Parser | Bank Statement Parser
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Frequently Asked Questions

Questions? Answers.

Does Bank Statement Parser send data to any remote server?

No. Bank Statement Parser is 100% self-contained and operates entirely on your local machine or server. It makes zero network calls and has zero telemetry.

Which formats are supported?

PDF (digital and scanned with OCR), CSV (auto-dialect), OFX (1.x and 2.x), QIF, SWIFT MT940/MT942, and ISO 20022 CAMT.053 XML.

Can I use Bank Statement Parser in commercial products?

Yes. Bank Statement Parser is dual-licensed under Apache-2.0 and MIT, allowing unrestricted commercial use.

entries.title: Getting Started with Bank Statement Parser: Installation & Quickstart | Bank Statement Parser
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Getting Started with Bank Statement Parser

Bank Statement Parser is distributed as a standalone command-line binary (CLI), a high-assurance Rust crate, and a native Python package.

1. Installation

Option A: Install via Cargo (Rust)

cargo install bankstatementparser

Option B: Install via Pip (Python)

pip install bankstatementparser

Option C: Run via Docker

docker pull ghcr.io/sebastienrousseau/bankstatementparser:latest docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data ghcr.io/sebastienrousseau/bankstatementparser:latest --input /data/statement.pdf

2. Command Line Interface (CLI) Usage

Parse a Single Statement

# Extract to standard JSON bankstatementparser --input statement.pdf --output statement.json # Extract to CSV bankstatementparser --input statement.ofx --output statement.csv --format csv # Extract to ISO 20022 CAMT.053 XML bankstatementparser --input statement.pdf --output statement.xml --format camt053

entries.content:
Skip to main content

Security Architecture & Trust Guarantees

Financial statement data requires the highest level of confidentiality and privacy assurance.

Core Security Pillars

1. 100% Zero-Telemetry Guarantee

Bank Statement Parser contains no analytics SDKs, no tracking pixels, and no remote crash reporters. The binary makes zero outbound network calls, making it ideal for air-gapped sovereign environments.

2. Rust Memory Safety

Engineered in 100% safe Rust without unverified unsafe pointer arithmetic. Immune to buffer overflows, dangling pointers, and memory corruption vulnerabilities common in legacy C/C++ parsers.

3. Subresource Integrity & Supply Chain Provenance

Every release build is signed using Sigstore Cosign and accompanied by a CycloneDX Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for verifiable dependency auditing.

entries.content:

Enterprise Use Cases & Deployment Patterns

High-throughput statement extraction powers critical automated financial backends.

Use Case 1

Corporate Treasury Automation

Consolidate disparate statements from 20+ global banking partners into a unified daily cash position. Automatically feeds ISO 20022 camt.053 feeds into SAP, Oracle NetSuite, and Kyriba TMS.

Use Case 2

Automated Bank Reconciliation

Match line-item transaction deposits against general ledger invoices. The deterministic tokenizer normalizes reference codes and cleans payee descriptions for 99.8% match rates.

Use Case 3

Fintech SME Credit Underwriting

Ingest 12–24 months of applicant PDF statements in milliseconds. Calculate monthly net operating cashflows, recurring subscription burn, and overdraft frequency with zero human keying.

Use Case 4

Forensic Audit & Sanctions Screening

Extract all counterparty names, IBANs, and transaction narratives across thousands of historic statements. Stream clean transaction metadata directly into anti-money laundering (AML) screening graphs.
